title: [Bugs] SMContext, UE IP and TEIDs leaked when PDU session establishment reject fails after the 201 response
body:
## Bug Description
`HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate` returns `201 Created` with a `Location` header as soon as it has handed PFCP session setup to a goroutine. If that setup then fails, `EstHandler` calls `sendPDUSessionEstablishmentReject` to tear the context down, but that function has three early returns before the one call that actually releases it, at the very end.

Taking any of the three leaves the SMContext registered in all three package-level maps, with its UE IP address and four TEIDs still allocated. Because the `201` already went out, the AMF believes the session was created and has no reason to send a release.

Reproduced below with no change to the leaking code: an association-only PFCP responder plus an absent AMF is enough. 31 requests leave 31 SMContexts, 31 `canonicalRef` entries, 31 `seidSMContextMap` entries and 31 UE IP addresses held, with zero `Release IP` log lines.

`sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept` has the same shape with four early returns and no release call at all.

**Acquire.** `NewSMContext` registers into `smContextPool` and `canonicalRef`, and into `seidSMContextMap` once PFCP context exists:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L282-L284

```go
smContext.Ref = uuid.New().URN()
smContextPool.Store(smContext.Ref, smContext)
canonicalRef.Store(canonicalName(id, pduSessID), smContext.Ref)
```

**Release.** `RemoveSMContext` clears all three maps and returns the UE IP and four TEIDs:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L397-L426

```go
ReleaseUEIP(smContext.SelectedUPF, smContext.PDUAddress, smContext.UseStaticIP)
for _, pfcpSessionContext := range smContext.PFCPContext {
    seidSMContextMap.Delete(pfcpSessionContext.LocalSEID)
}
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeidForSplitPDUSession)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeidForSplitPDUSession)
smContextPool.Delete(ref)
canonicalRef.Delete(canonicalName(smContext.Supi, smContext.PDUSessionID))
```

Its only caller is `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`, so missing that call means the context is never released.

**The response goes out before anything can fail.** PFCP setup is handed to a goroutine and the handler answers immediately:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L291-L306

```go
needUnlock = false
go func() {
    defer smContext.SMLock.Unlock()
    smContext.SendUpPathChgNotification("EARLY", SendUpPathChgEventExposureNotification)
    handler := func(smContext *smf_context.SMContext, success bool) {
        p.EstHandler(isDone, smContext, success)
    }
    ActivateUPFSession(smContext, handler)
    ...
}()
```

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L330-L331

```go
c.Header("Location", location)
c.JSON(http.StatusCreated, response)
```

By the time the goroutine can fail, the AMF already holds a `201` and a `smContextRef`.

**Where the release is skipped.** A failed PFCP establishment gives `success = false`, and `EstHandler` routes to the reject path:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/datapath.go#L250-L263

```go
if success {
    p.sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept(smContext)
} else {
    p.sendPDUSessionEstablishmentReject(smContext, nasMessage.Cause5GSMNetworkFailure)
}
```

That function exists to tear the context down, yet the teardown is its last statement and three returns precede it:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/datapath.go#L269-L308

```go
smNasBuf, err := smf_context.BuildGSMPDUSessionEstablishmentReject(
    smContext, nasMessage.Cause5GSMNetworkFailure)
if err != nil {
    logger.PduSessLog.Errorf("Build GSM PDUSessionEstablishmentReject failed: %s", err)
    return                                        // L276: no release
}
...
ctx, _, errToken := smf_context.GetSelf().GetTokenCtx(
    models.ServiceName_NAMF_COMM, models.NrfNfManagementNfType_AMF)
if errToken != nil {
    logger.PduSessLog.Warnf("Get NAMF_COMM context failed: %s", errToken)
    return                                        // L295: no release
}
rspData, err := p.Consumer().
    N1N2MessageTransfer(ctx, smContext.Supi, n1n2Request, smContext.CommunicationClientApiPrefix)
if err != nil || rspData == nil {
    logger.ConsumerLog.Warnf("N1N2MessageTransfer for SendPDUSessionEstablishmentReject failed: %+v", err)
    return                                        // L301: no release
}
...
p.RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, true)       // L307: the only release
```

This path runs after UPF selection and IP allocation, so the UE IP and TEIDs are already assigned and leak along with the map entries.

**The accept path has the same shape.** `sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept` has four early returns and no release call anywhere:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/datapath.go#L308-L369

Not releasing on success is correct, but a token or `N1N2MessageTransfer` failure means nothing reached the AMF while the context stays registered. Same defect, should be fixed in the same change.

## To Reproduce
free5gc v4.2.2, SMF v1.4.3. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, subscriber `imsi-208930000000001`, DNN `internet`, `oauth: true`. Only source change is an `AuthorizationCheck` bypass so `curl` can stand in for an AMF; `datapath.go`, `NewSMContext` and `RemoveSMContext` are untouched.

Two ordinary failures are needed. The UPF must be associated but unresponsive to session messages: a ~90-line UDP stub answers Association Setup and Heartbeat, ignores Session Establishment. (With no UPF at all, selection skips it and the create fails earlier on a path that releases correctly.) The AMF is simply not started, so `GetTokenCtx(NAMF_COMM, AMF)` fails.

A probe in the SMF runs `runtime.GC()` and reports the three map sizes, so anything still counted is reachable state.

**The leak, one request:**

    http=201                                        <- AMF is told the session exists
    Location: .../sm-contexts/cd02218a-0ba0-4e97-9ff4-b4e7a602cc6c
    probe now    : smContextPool 1, canonicalRef 1, seidSMContextMap 1
    probe at 15s : smContextPool 1, canonicalRef 1, seidSMContextMap 1

What happened in between:

    [INFO] Allocated UE IP address: 10.60.0.1
    [INFO] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request
    [INFO] | 201 | POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts     <- response already sent
       ... 9 s later, in the goroutine ...
    [WARN] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request error: retry-out
    [WARN] Get NAMF_COMM context failed: server no response  <- L294, returns at L295

L307 is never reached. No `is deleted from pool`, no `Release IP`. The context, its IP and its TEIDs stay held while the AMF believes the session is up.

**Control, same setup:** remove the subscriber policy from the PCF and the create fails at `ApplySessionRules`, before the goroutine:

    [INFO] UE[imsi-...] PDUSessionID[1] Release IP[10.60.0.2]
    [INFO] smContext[urn:uuid:5ea46820-...] is deleted from pool

Same request, same code, released properly. Only the post-`201` async path leaks.

**Accumulation, 31 requests** — `pduSessionId` incrementing:

| requests | smContextPool | canonicalRef | seidSMContextMap | heap objects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 26,553 |
| 20 | 20 | 20 | 20 | 29,465 |
| 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 32,387 |
| 31, after forced GC | 31 | 31 | 31 | 32,730 |

Slope exactly 1 per request across all three maps, no ceiling, unchanged by `runtime.GC()`.

    'retry-out'                     31   every PFCP establishment failed
    'Get NAMF_COMM context failed'  31   every one reached L294
    'Allocated UE IP address'       31
    'Release IP'                     0   31 addresses out, none back

## Expected Behavior
When the reject path takes any early return (L276, L295, L301), and likewise when the accept path fails on a token or `N1N2MessageTransfer` error, the handler should still release the SMContext via `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF` before returning, so the context, its UE IP and its TEIDs are not leaked.

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
 - free5GC Version: v4.2.2 (SMF v1.4.3, `2232d299`)
 - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
 - Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
 - go version: go1.27.0 linux/amd64
 - C compiler version (optional):

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files
N/A — default config with only `oauth: true` set. Reproduction conditions are described above.

### PCAP File
N/A — this is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

### Log File

    [INFO] Allocated UE IP address: 10.60.0.1
    [INFO] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request
    [INFO] | 201 | POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts
    [WARN] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request error: retry-out
    [WARN] Get NAMF_COMM context failed: server no response

## System Architecture (Optional)
Bare metal, single host. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, UPF replaced by an association-only UDP stub.

## Walkthrough (Optional)
The reject path runs after UPF selection and IP allocation, so the UE IP and TEIDs are already assigned and leak along with the map entries. The IP pool binds long before memory does: a `/24` DNN pool holds 254 addresses, so a few hundred leaked contexts exhaust it and new sessions are refused for the whole DNN while `free -m` still looks fine.

## Additional Context
Each create that reaches the reject path and takes L276, L295 or L301 permanently holds one entry in each of the three maps, the SMContext itself (thirteen maps, four ID generators, a BPManager, two UPTunnels, roughly 80 heap objects in the measured run), one UE IP address and four TEIDs.

The AMF does hold `smContextRef` from the `201`, so a release is not structurally impossible the way it is when the identifier is never sent. But the AMF was told the session succeeded and has no reason to release it, and in this scenario the AMF is itself unreachable. In practice these contexts persist until the SMF restarts or a create with the same SUPI and PDU session id reclaims them.

State also diverges three ways: the AMF and UE believe a session exists, the UPF has no session installed, and the SMF holds a context it failed to tear down.
